title: Canonical derived tensor internal-Hom bijection
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] and its shared derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Define the canonical family $e_{K,L,M}:\operatorname{Hom}(K,R\mathcal Hom(L,M))\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(K\otimes^L L,M)$, natural in all three variables [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-adjunction], as follows. Fix the same functorial K-injective resolution $\eta_M:M\to I(M)$ as the recorded derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Let $j_{L,M}:R\mathcal Hom(QL,QM)\simeq Q\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L,I(M))$ be its localization factorization. For a K-flat complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], arbitrary complexes $L,M$, and every chain map $\phi:P\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L,I(M))$ [def-pur-hom-complex], require a chain map $\psi:\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes L)\to I(M)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] whose restriction to each summand $P^p\otimes L^q$ is the uncurrying of $\phi^p$ projected to $\mathcal Hom(L^q,I(M)^{p+q})$, with tensor symmetry restoring the order [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. This is the componentwise evaluation construction underlying [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total]. Require $e_{QP,QL,QM}(Q\phi;j_{L,M}^{-1})=\mu_X(P,L);Q\psi;(Q\eta_M)^{-1}$, where $\mu_X$ is the actual localization tensor model map [def-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-comparison]. Naturality and this equation determine the family uniquely; choose the family supplied by the named existence theorem.

proof.text: Existence remains open: use K-flat representatives of both tensor inputs and the fixed K-injective replacement of the target. The componentwise tensor-Hom adjunction produces the uncurried chain maps; common resolutions give a natural family compatible with the localization tensor model map. This is the argument still required by exists_canonicalDerivedTensorHom.

For uniqueness, choose K-flat resolutions P and Lc of complex representatives of K and L using lem-pc-kflat-resolution. Their quasi-isomorphisms give isomorphisms a:QP≅K and b:QLc≅L; essential surjectivity gives c:QMc≅M. The fixed replacement I(Mc) is K-injective, and lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective makes Hom(Lc,I(Mc)) K-injective.

Transport f:K→RHom(L,M) to g:QP→RHom(QLc,QMc), then compose with the fixed resolution-factorization isomorphism j. The K-injective localization Hom bijection (lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived) lifts this to the homotopy category; quotient fullness lifts further to a chain map φ. Naturality of quotientCompQhIso and cancellation give Qφ;j⁻¹=g.

Apply each family’s representative clause to φ. Its two uncurried maps ψ and ψ′ have equal restriction to every tensor summand, since both restrictions equal schemeTensorHomUncurryComponent. HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor.hom_ext followed by HomologicalComplex.hom_ext gives ψ=ψ′. Their coordinate equations therefore give equal values at g.

Use the two naturality clauses at a.hom, b.hom and c.inv to identify the equal coordinate values with (a.hom⊗b.hom);e(f);c.inv and (a.hom⊗b.hom);e′(f);c.inv. Cancel the tensor of the two isomorphisms and c.inv. Function and Equiv extensionality give e=e′.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08DJ; uniqueness formalized using sites-cohomology Tag 0A96 and Mathlib KInjective.Qh_map_bijective. Existence remains open.
